import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 38

*Reference:*
- [erdosproblems.com/38](https://www.erdosproblems.com/38)
- [Er56](Erdős, P., Problems and results in additive number theory.
  Colloque sur la Théorie des Nombres, Bruxelles, 1955 (1956), 127-137.)
-/

open Set Pointwise

namespace Erdos38

open scoped Classical in
/--
Does there exist $B \subset \mathbb{N}$ which is not an additive basis,
but is such that for every set $A \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ of Schnirelmann density $\alpha$
and every $N$ there exists $b \in B$ such that
$$
  \lvert (A \cup (A+b)) \cap \{1, \ldots, N\} \rvert \geq (\alpha + f(\alpha)) N
$$
where $f(\alpha) > 0$ for $0 < \alpha < 1$?

Note: here Erdős seems to use a slightly weaker notion of an additive basis (see [Er56] at the top
of page 135). In particular, for this problem, a set is an additive basis of order $k$ if every
natural number can be written as a sum of _at most_ $k$ elements of the set, rather than as a sum of
_precisely_ $k$ elements.

A positive [solution](https://github.com/spicylemonade/erdos-38) was given by GPT 5.5 Pro
(prompted by gebyjaff, cleanup by Liam Price); in fact a sparse random set $B$ has this property,
with $f(\alpha)\gg \alpha (1-\alpha)^2$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using lean4 at
"https://www.erdosproblems.com/forum/thread/38#post-6131"]
theorem erdos_38 : answer(True) ↔
    ∃ B : Set ℕ, ¬ B.IsWeakAddBasis ∧ ∃ f : ℝ → ℝ, (∀ α, 0 < α → α < 1 → f α > 0) ∧
      ∀ (A : Set ℕ) (N : ℕ),
        let α := schnirelmannDensity A
        ∃ b ∈ B, (Ioc 0 N ∩ (A ∪ (A + {b}))).ncard ≥ (α + f α) * N := by
  sorry

end Erdos38

reformulations.difference: The density-increment clause includes N = 0 and densities 0 and 1, whereas Theorem 1 of the cited solution states the substantive assertion for N ≥ 1 and 0 < α < 1.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Restricting the Lean assertion gives the interior-density version. Conversely, extend an interior witness f by zero outside (0,1). For either endpoint, |A ∩ {1,…,N}| ≥ schnirelmannDensity(A)·N, and adjoining a translate cannot decrease this count. At N = 0 both sides vanish. The interior assertion already forces B to be nonempty, by applying it to the odd numbers. The equivalence between the two existential-f formulations was proved in /workspace/review/endpoints.lean as Review38.endpoint_equivalence_without_nonempty.

sources_consulted: Erdős, P., Problems and results in additive number theory (1956), especially pp. 134–136: https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1956-17.pdf
Erdős bibliography identifying the cited paper: https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/Erdos.html

Cited solution repository: https://github.com/spicylemonade/erdos-38; its paper, A Resolution of Erdős Problem 38, Theorem 1 and proof: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/spicylemonade/erdos-38/main/38.pdf

Erdős Problems, discussion thread 38, read through https://r.jina.ai/https://www.erdosproblems.com/forum/thread/38 (the mirror preserved prose and status but omitted formulas and some discussion content).

review.notes: The main theorem faithfully states Erdős’s question. Page 135 explicitly defines a basis using 'k or fewer' summands, matching IsWeakAddBasis. The counted set is always finite, so ncard’s infinite-set default is unreachable. Lean checks confirmed the density boundary cases, genuine iterated sumset semantics, invariance under restricting A to positive integers, and that any witness B must contain 1. The available forum mirror records 'PROVED (LEAN)' and an affirmative solution, consistent with research solved and answer(True). Scratch equivalence and boundary proofs use no sorry axioms. The reviewed file matches its committed blob; no repository files were edited.
